5	/-
6	  TrafficSpec.Core.Runtime.Grounding
7	  Which assignments of tracks to binders exist over a trace, how a broken track is followed, and
8	  the per-grounding timeline of verdicts.
9	
10	  A track is a source's identity, not an object's. When a tracker breaks and the adapter claims a
11	  continuation (`Scene.links`, old ↦ new), the trace is rewritten once to canonical identities
12	  when the break is shorter than the manifest's re-identification gap; the instants inside the gap
13	  are unknown (identityGap), never a fresh party. A binder whose track is not present at an
14	  instant outside any gap leaves the rule not engaged there: the other party has left the scene.
15	
16	  Groundings are tuples of distinct candidates that are co-present at some instant; each
17	  grounding evaluates the rule once over the whole trace, and formulas that depend on a subset of
18	  the binders are shared across the groundings that agree on that subset.
19	
20	  Rules never import this file: a rule that could see the census of tracks could special-case it.
21	-/
22	import TrafficSpec.Core.Language.RuleEval
23	import TrafficSpec.Core.Runtime.Admission
24	
25	namespace TrafficSpec
26	namespace Grounding
27	open Semantics
28	
29	/-- An assignment of canonical tracks to binder names, and of regions to the variables a
30	    concept's instance takes as region formals (a rule's groundings bind none). -/
31	structure Grounding where
32	  assign : List (String × TrackId)
33	  regions : List (String × RegionId) := []
34	  deriving Repr, DecidableEq, Inhabited
35	
36	def Grounding.render (g : Grounding) : String :=
37	  String.intercalate "," (g.assign.map fun (n, t) => s!"{n}={t}")
38	def Grounding.binding (g : Grounding) : Binding :=
39	  ⟨g.assign.map (fun (n, t) => (n, Val.track t)) ++ g.regions.map fun (n, r) => (n, Val.region r)⟩
40	
41	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
42	-- Identity: canonical tracks through accepted links, applied to the trace once
43	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
44	/-- The scene with every track id replaced by its canonical identity. -/
45	def canonicalScene (cm : List (TrackId × TrackId)) (s : Scene) : Scene :=
46	  let c := canon cm
47	  { s with
48	    subject := s.subject.map c
49	    users := s.users.map fun u => { u with track := c u.track }
50	    occupancyObserved := s.occupancyObserved.map c
51	    occupies := s.occupies.map fun (t, r) => (c t, r)
52	    relations := s.relations.map fun m => { m with a := c m.a, b := c m.b }
53	    intents := s.intents.map fun d => { d with vehicle := c d.vehicle } }
54	
55	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
56	-- Setup: the canonical, indexed trace and the rule set
57	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
58	structure Setup where
59	  rules : List Rule
60	  d : Primitives.Ctx
61	  gap : Q
62	  cm : List (TrackId × TrackId) := []
63	
64	def Setup.mk' (rules : List Rule) (τ : Trace) (ρ : Reading) (gap : Q) : Setup :=
65	  let arr := τ.toArray
66	  let cm := canonMap arr gap
67	  { rules := rules, d := Primitives.Ctx.mk' (τ.map (canonicalScene cm)) ρ, gap := gap, cm := cm }
68	
69	/-- The setup of a trace every evaluation reaches: built only when `Admission.defects` finds no
70	    defect in the trace as written, else the defects. -/
71	def Setup.admit (rules : List Rule) (τ : Trace) (ρ : Reading) (gap : Q) : Except (List String) Setup :=
72	  match Admission.defects τ gap with
73	  | [] => .ok (Setup.mk' rules τ ρ gap)
74	  | ds => .error ds
75	
76	def Setup.n (S : Setup) : Nat := S.d.n
77	def Setup.scenes (S : Setup) : Array Scene := S.d.scenes
78	def Setup.ctx (S : Setup) (β : Binding) : SemCtx := Rule.context S.rules S.d β
79	def Setup.tracks (S : Setup) : List TrackId := (S.scenes.toList.flatMap (·.tracks)).eraseDups
80	/-- First and last instant at which a canonical identity is present. -/
81	def Setup.span (S : Setup) (t : TrackId) : Option (Nat × Nat) :=
82	  match firstSeen S.scenes t, lastSeen S.scenes t with
83	  | some a, some b => some (a, b)
84	  | _, _ => none
85	
86	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
87	-- Enumeration
88	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
89	/-- Tracks that satisfy a binder's class at some instant (evaluated once per track). -/
90	def candidates (S : Setup) (b : Binder) : List TrackId :=
91	  S.tracks.filter fun t =>
92	    (Rule.evalRuleFormula (S.ctx ⟨[(b.name, .track t)]⟩) b.cls).any fun r => r.v == .t
93	
94	def spansOverlap (S : Setup) (a b : TrackId) : Bool :=
95	  match S.span a, S.span b with
96	  | some (a0, a1), some (b0, b1) => a0 ≤ b1 && b0 ≤ a1
97	  | _, _ => false
98	
99	/-- All assignments of distinct, pairwise co-present candidates to the binders, subject first.
100	    Each binder's candidates are computed once. -/
101	def groundings (S : Setup) (r : Rule) : List Grounding :=
102	  let cands := r.binders.map fun b => (b.name, candidates S b)
103	  let rec go (bs : List (String × List TrackId)) (used : List TrackId) : List (List (String × TrackId)) :=
104	    match bs with
105	    | [] => [[]]
106	    | (name, cs) :: rest =>
107	      cs.filter (fun c => !used.contains c && used.all (spansOverlap S c)) |>.flatMap fun c =>
108	        (go rest (c :: used)).map fun tail => (name, c) :: tail
109	  (go cands []).map fun a => { assign := a }
110	
111	/-- Predicted grounding count without enumerating: the product of candidate counts (an upper
112	    bound when candidates overlap). -/
113	def predictedGroundings (S : Setup) (r : Rule) : Nat :=
114	  r.binders.foldl (fun acc b => acc * (candidates S b).length) 1
115	
116	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
117	-- Timelines
118	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
119	/-- One evaluation of a rule for a grounding: the verdict per instant, whether the rule was
120	    engaged at some instant with every party present, and whether every party was present at
121	    some instant at all. -/
122	structure Timeline where
123	  verdicts : Array (Timestamp × Verdict)
124	  live : Bool
125	  present : Bool
126	  deriving Repr
127	
128	/-- Evaluate a rule for a grounding once. A binder absent inside its identity's span is an
129	    identity gap (unknown); absent outside it, the rule is not engaged. -/
130	def evaluate (S : Setup) (r : Rule) (g : Grounding) : Timeline :=
131	  let c := S.ctx g.binding
132	  let engaged := r.engagedAll c
133	  let obl := Rule.evalRuleFormula c r.obligation
134	  let spans := g.assign.map fun (_, t) => (t, S.span t)
135	  let rows := (Array.range S.n).map fun i =>
136	    let s := S.scenes[i]!
137	    let missing := spans.filter fun (t, _) => !s.tracks.contains t
138	    let v : Verdict :=
139	      if missing.isEmpty then verdictAt engaged[i]! obl[i]!
140	      else
141	        let inGap := missing.filter fun (_, sp) => match sp with
142	          | some (a, b) => a < i && i < b
143	          | none => false
144	        if inGap.isEmpty then .notApplicable
145	        else .unknown (inGap.map fun (t, _) => .identityGap t)
146	    (s.t, v, missing.isEmpty && engaged[i]!.v == .t, missing.isEmpty)
147	  ⟨rows.map fun (t, v, _, _) => (t, v), rows.any fun (_, _, l, _) => l, rows.any fun (_, _, _, p) => p⟩
148	
149	def timeline (S : Setup) (r : Rule) (g : Grounding) : Array (Timestamp × Verdict) := (evaluate S r g).verdicts
150	
151	/-- The verdict of a grounding at one instant. -/
152	def verdictAt (S : Setup) (r : Rule) (g : Grounding) (i : Nat) : Verdict :=
153	  ((timeline S r g)[i]?).map (·.2) |>.getD (.unknown [.outOfRange])
154	
155	/-- The episode verdict: a violation anywhere is a violation; else any unknown is unknown (with
156	    every reason); else engaged anywhere is compliant; else not applicable. -/
157	def episode (tl : List Verdict) : Verdict :=
158	  if tl.any (· == .violated) then .violated
159	  else
160	    let unknowns := tl.flatMap Verdict.reasons
161	    if tl.any (fun v => match v with | .unknown _ => true | _ => false) then .unknown unknowns.eraseDups
162	    else if tl.any (· == .compliant) then .compliant
163	    else .notApplicable
164	
165	/-- Every grounding evaluated once: its episode verdict and timeline. -/
166	def check (S : Setup) (r : Rule) : List (Grounding × Timeline × Verdict) :=
167	  (groundings S r).map fun g =>
168	    let tl := evaluate S r g
169	    (g, tl, episode (tl.verdicts.toList.map (·.2)))
170	
171	/-- Engaged (applicability true) at some instant for some grounding: the rule says something on
172	    this trace. -/
173	def live (S : Setup) (r : Rule) : Bool := (check S r).any fun (_, tl, _) => tl.live
174	
175	end Grounding
176	end TrafficSpec

  atoms the split omits are removed. Do not edit; regenerate.
-/
/-
  TrafficSpec.Core.Runtime.Grounding
  Which assignments of tracks to binders exist over a trace, how a broken track is followed, and
  the per-grounding timeline of verdicts.

  A track is a source's identity, not an object's. When a tracker breaks and the adapter claims a
  continuation (`Scene.links`, old ↦ new), the trace is rewritten once to canonical identities
  when the break is shorter than the manifest's re-identification gap; the instants inside the gap
  are unknown (identityGap), never a fresh party. A binder whose track is not present at an
  instant outside any gap leaves the rule not engaged there: the other party has left the scene.

  Groundings are tuples of distinct candidates that are co-present at some instant; each
  grounding evaluates the rule once over the whole trace, and formulas that depend on a subset of
  the binders are shared across the groundings that agree on that subset.

  Rules never import this file: a rule that could see the census of tracks could special-case it.
-/
import TrafficSpec.Core.Language.RuleEval
import TrafficSpec.Core.Runtime.Admission

namespace TrafficSpec
namespace Grounding
open Semantics

/-- An assignment of canonical tracks to binder names, and of regions to the variables a
    concept's instance takes as region formals (a rule's groundings bind none). -/
structure Grounding where
  assign : List (String × TrackId)
  regions : List (String × RegionId) := []
  deriving Repr, DecidableEq, Inhabited

def Grounding.render (g : Grounding) : String :=
  String.intercalate "," (g.assign.map fun (n, t) => s!"{n}={t}")
def Grounding.binding (g : Grounding) : Binding :=
  ⟨g.assign.map (fun (n, t) => (n, Val.track t)) ++ g.regions.map fun (n, r) => (n, Val.region r)⟩

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Identity: canonical tracks through accepted links, applied to the trace once
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
/-- The scene with every track id replaced by its canonical identity. -/
def canonicalScene (cm : List (TrackId × TrackId)) (s : Scene) : Scene :=
  let c := canon cm
  { s with
    subject := s.subject.map c
    users := s.users.map fun u => { u with track := c u.track }
    occupancyObserved := s.occupancyObserved.map c
    occupies := s.occupies.map fun (t, r) => (c t, r)
    relations := s.relations.map fun m => { m with a := c m.a, b := c m.b }
    intents := s.intents.map fun d => { d with vehicle := c d.vehicle } }

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Setup: the canonical, indexed trace and the rule set
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
structure Setup where
  rules : List Rule
  d : Primitives.Ctx
  gap : Q
  cm : List (TrackId × TrackId) := []

def Setup.mk' (rules : List Rule) (τ : Trace) (ρ : Reading) (gap : Q) : Setup :=
  let arr := τ.toArray
  let cm := canonMap arr gap
  { rules := rules, d := Primitives.Ctx.mk' (τ.map (canonicalScene cm)) ρ, gap := gap, cm := cm }

/-- The setup of a trace every evaluation reaches: built only when `Admission.defects` finds no
    defect in the trace as written, else the defects. -/
def Setup.admit (rules : List Rule) (τ : Trace) (ρ : Reading) (gap : Q) : Except (List String) Setup :=
  match Admission.defects τ gap with
  | [] => .ok (Setup.mk' rules τ ρ gap)
  | ds => .error ds

def Setup.n (S : Setup) : Nat := S.d.n
def Setup.scenes (S : Setup) : Array Scene := S.d.scenes
def Setup.ctx (S : Setup) (β : Binding) : SemCtx := Rule.context S.rules S.d β
def Setup.tracks (S : Setup) : List TrackId := (S.scenes.toList.flatMap (·.tracks)).eraseDups
/-- First and last instant at which a canonical identity is present. -/
def Setup.span (S : Setup) (t : TrackId) : Option (Nat × Nat) :=
  match firstSeen S.scenes t, lastSeen S.scenes t with
  | some a, some b => some (a, b)
  | _, _ => none

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Enumeration
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
/-- Tracks that satisfy a binder's class at some instant (evaluated once per track). -/
def candidates (S : Setup) (b : Binder) : List TrackId :=
  S.tracks.filter fun t =>
    (Rule.evalRuleFormula (S.ctx ⟨[(b.name, .track t)]⟩) b.cls).any fun r => r.v == .t

def spansOverlap (S : Setup) (a b : TrackId) : Bool :=
  match S.span a, S.span b with
  | some (a0, a1), some (b0, b1) => a0 ≤ b1 && b0 ≤ a1
  | _, _ => false

/-- All assignments of distinct, pairwise co-present candidates to the binders, subject first.
    Each binder's candidates are computed once. -/
def groundings (S : Setup) (r : Rule) : List Grounding :=
  let cands := r.binders.map fun b => (b.name, candidates S b)
  let rec go (bs : List (String × List TrackId)) (used : List TrackId) : List (List (String × TrackId)) :=
    match bs with
    | [] => [[]]
    | (name, cs) :: rest =>
      cs.filter (fun c => !used.contains c && used.all (spansOverlap S c)) |>.flatMap fun c =>
        (go rest (c :: used)).map fun tail => (name, c) :: tail
  (go cands []).map fun a => { assign := a }

/-- Predicted grounding count without enumerating: the product of candidate counts (an upper
    bound when candidates overlap). -/
def predictedGroundings (S : Setup) (r : Rule) : Nat :=
  r.binders.foldl (fun acc b => acc * (candidates S b).length) 1

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Timelines
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
/-- One evaluation of a rule for a grounding: the verdict per instant, whether the rule was
    engaged at some instant with every party present, and whether every party was present at
    some instant at all. -/
structure Timeline where
  verdicts : Array (Timestamp × Verdict)
  live : Bool
  present : Bool
  deriving Repr

/-- Evaluate a rule for a grounding once. A binder absent inside its identity's span is an
    identity gap (unknown); absent outside it, the rule is not engaged. -/
def evaluate (S : Setup) (r : Rule) (g : Grounding) : Timeline :=
  let c := S.ctx g.binding
  let engaged := r.engagedAll c
  let obl := Rule.evalRuleFormula c r.obligation
  let spans := g.assign.map fun (_, t) => (t, S.span t)
  let rows := (Array.range S.n).map fun i =>
    let s := S.scenes[i]!
    let missing := spans.filter fun (t, _) => !s.tracks.contains t
    let v : Verdict :=
      if missing.isEmpty then verdictAt engaged[i]! obl[i]!
      else
        let inGap := missing.filter fun (_, sp) => match sp with
          | some (a, b) => a < i && i < b
          | none => false
        if inGap.isEmpty then .notApplicable
        else .unknown (inGap.map fun (t, _) => .identityGap t)
    (s.t, v, missing.isEmpty && engaged[i]!.v == .t, missing.isEmpty)
  ⟨rows.map fun (t, v, _, _) => (t, v), rows.any fun (_, _, l, _) => l, rows.any fun (_, _, _, p) => p⟩

def timeline (S : Setup) (r : Rule) (g : Grounding) : Array (Timestamp × Verdict) := (evaluate S r g).verdicts

/-- The verdict of a grounding at one instant. -/
def verdictAt (S : Setup) (r : Rule) (g : Grounding) (i : Nat) : Verdict :=
  ((timeline S r g)[i]?).map (·.2) |>.getD (.unknown [.outOfRange])

/-- The episode verdict: a violation anywhere is a violation; else any unknown is unknown (with
    every reason); else engaged anywhere is compliant; else not applicable. -/
def episode (tl : List Verdict) : Verdict :=
  if tl.any (· == .violated) then .violated
  else
    let unknowns := tl.flatMap Verdict.reasons
    if tl.any (fun v => match v with | .unknown _ => true | _ => false) then .unknown unknowns.eraseDups
    else if tl.any (· == .compliant) then .compliant
    else .notApplicable

/-- Every grounding evaluated once: its episode verdict and timeline. -/
def check (S : Setup) (r : Rule) : List (Grounding × Timeline × Verdict) :=
  (groundings S r).map fun g =>
    let tl := evaluate S r g
    (g, tl, episode (tl.verdicts.toList.map (·.2)))

/-- Engaged (applicability true) at some instant for some grounding: the rule says something on
    this trace. -/
def live (S : Setup) (r : Rule) : Bool := (check S r).any fun (_, tl, _) => tl.live

end Grounding
end TrafficSpec

/-
  TrafficSpec.Core.Runtime.Admission
  What a trace must satisfy, as written, before any rule is evaluated on it: the declared facts
  (assumptions and intentions) name what their scene holds, each once, by well-formed ids; no
  structure is labelled with an abstract kind or lists one among the kinds its source cannot tell
  (an abstract kind is the union of the kinds refining it, read only by a formula); and the
  accepted re-identification links are one-to-one.

  The checks are exact and read no geometry, so a recorded trace, a JSON case and a Lean witness
  are held to them alike. `Grounding.Setup.admit` calls them; every evaluation builds its setup
  there.
-/
import TrafficSpec.Core.Runtime.Identity
import TrafficSpec.Core.Vocab.Assumptions
import TrafficSpec.Core.Vocab.Intentions

namespace TrafficSpec
namespace Admission

private def duplicates {α : Type} [BEq α] (xs : List α) : List α :=
  (xs.filter fun x => xs.count x > 1).eraseDups

/-- The defects of one scene's declared facts. -/
def sceneDefects (s : Scene) : List String :=
  let at_ := s!"scene t={s.t}"
  (s.intents.flatMap fun d =>
    let who := s!"{at_}: intent record ({d.vehicle}, {d.target})"
    (if s.tracks.contains d.vehicle then [] else [s!"{who}: vehicle {d.vehicle} is not a road user of the scene"]) ++
    (if (s.structure? d.target).isSome then [] else [s!"{who}: target {d.target} is not a structure of the scene"]) ++
    ((duplicates (d.values.map (·.1))).map fun id => s!"{who}: `{id}` listed more than once") ++
    ((d.values.map (·.1)).eraseDups.filter (!IntId.wellFormed ·) |>.map fun id => s!"{who}: `{id}` is not a well-formed intention id")) ++
  ((duplicates (s.intents.map fun d => (d.vehicle, d.target))).map fun (v, r) => s!"{at_}: more than one intent record for ({v}, {r})") ++
  (s.structures.flatMap fun st =>
    (if st.kind.isAbstract then [s!"{at_}: structure {st.id} is labelled `{st.kind}`, an abstract kind; label it with a kind that refines `{st.kind}`"] else []) ++
    ((st.unobservedKinds.filter (·.isAbstract)).eraseDups.map fun k =>
      s!"{at_}: structure {st.id} lists `{k}` among unobserved_kinds, an abstract kind; list the kinds refining it that the source cannot tell")) ++
  ((duplicates (s.assumptions.map (·.1))).map fun id => s!"{at_}: assumption `{id}` listed more than once") ++
  ((s.assumptions.map (·.1)).eraseDups.filter (!AsmId.wellFormed ·) |>.map fun id => s!"{at_}: `{id}` is not a well-formed assumption id")

/-- Accepted links that give a track two successors or two predecessors. -/
def linkDefects (τ : Array Scene) (gap : Q) : List String :=
  let links := Grounding.acceptedLinks τ gap
  ((duplicates (links.map (·.1))).map fun t =>
    s!"track {t} is continued by more than one accepted link: {links.filter (·.1 == t)}") ++
  ((duplicates (links.map (·.2))).map fun t =>
    s!"track {t} continues more than one accepted link: {links.filter (·.2 == t)}")

/-- Every defect of the trace as written; empty for a trace every evaluation may read. -/
def defects (τ : Trace) (gap : Q) : List String :=
  τ.flatMap sceneDefects ++ linkDefects τ.toArray gap

end Admission
end TrafficSpec

111	-- Lifting scene functions over the trace; positions for windows
112	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
113	def each (c : Ctx) (f : Scene → R) : Array R := c.scenes.map f
114	def eachQ (c : Ctx) (f : Scene → QR) : Array QR := c.scenes.map f
115	def timePos (c : Ctx) : Array (Option Q) := c.times.map some
116	def pathPos (c : Ctx) (x : TrackId) : Array (Option Q) := c.scenes.map (kin_path_length · x)
117	def positions (c : Ctx) (m : Measure) (x : TrackId) : Array (Option Q) :=
118	  match m with | .time => timePos c | .path => pathPos c x
119	def missingPos (m : Measure) : UnknownReason :=
120	  match m with | .time => .outOfRange | .path => .absentAtom "kin_path_length"
121	
122	def bAtom (o : Option Bool) (name : String) : R := R.ofOption o (.absentAtom name)
123	def qAtom (o : Option Q) (name : String) : QR :=
124	  match o with | some q => .ok q | none => .error (.absentAtom name)
125	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
126	-- Scene-level helpers over atoms
127	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
128	/-- Heading change (degrees, left positive) integrated over the back window of length w:
129	    prefix sums of yaw rate × interval, one window query per instant. -/
130	def yawChange (c : Ctx) (x : TrackId) (w : Q) : Array (Except UnknownReason Q) :=
131	  let n := c.n
132	  -- sums[i] = Σ_{k ≤ i} ω_k (t_k − t_{k−1}); a missing yaw rate contributes nothing and is tracked
133	  let sums := (List.range n).foldl (fun (acc : Array Q) i =>
134	    let prev := if i = 0 then Q.zero else acc[i - 1]!
135	    let dt := if i = 0 then Q.zero else Q.sub c.times[i]! c.times[i - 1]!
136	    acc.push (match kin_yaw_rate c.scenes[i]! x with
137	      | some ω => Q.add prev (Q.mul ω dt)
138	      | none => prev)) #[]
139	  -- lastMissing[i] = latest index ≤ i with a missing yaw rate (n when none)
140	  let lastMissing := (List.range n).foldl (fun (acc : Array Nat) i =>
141	    acc.push (if (kin_yaw_rate c.scenes[i]! x).isNone then i else (if i = 0 then n else acc[i - 1]!))) #[]
142	  let wins := Time.backWindows (timePos c) w
143	  (Array.range n).map fun i =>
144	    match wins[i]! with
145	    | none => .error .outOfRange
146	    | some win =>
147	      if !win.covered then .error (.windowTruncated "prim_heading_change")
148	      else if !win.adequate then .error (.samplingGap "prim_heading_change")
149	      else
150	        let lm := lastMissing[i]!
151	        if lm ≠ n && lm > win.j0 then .error (.absentAtom "kin_yaw_rate")
152	        else .ok (Q.sub sums[i]! sums[win.j0]!)
153	
154	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
155	-- The primitives
156	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
157	/-- minute m of the day lies in the window [start, end), wrapping past midnight when end ≤ start. -/
158	def inWindow (w : TimeWindow) (m : Nat) : Bool :=
159	  if w.startMinute < w.endMinute then w.startMinute ≤ m && m < w.endMinute
160	  else m ≥ w.startMinute || m < w.endMinute
161	
162	private def hasClassOpt (s : Scene) (x : TrackId) (k : RoadUserClass) : Option Bool :=
163	  (s.user x).bind fun u => if u.unobservedClasses.contains k then none else u.classes.map (·.contains k)
164	
165	private def vecAtom (o : Option Vec) (name : String) : Except UnknownReason Vec :=
166	  match o with | some v => .ok v | none => .error (.absentAtom name)
167	
168	/-- Under constant velocities, the time of closest approach of the two centres and the centre
169	    distance then; `none` when the paths do not approach within `[0, horizon]`. -/
170	private def closestApproach (s : Scene) (a b : TrackId) (horizon : Q) : Except UnknownReason (Option (Q × Q)) := do
171	  let pa ← vecAtom (kin_position s a) "kin_position"
172	  let pb ← vecAtom (kin_position s b) "kin_position"
173	  let va ← vecAtom (kin_velocity s a) "kin_velocity"
174	  let vb ← vecAtom (kin_velocity s b) "kin_velocity"
175	  let r := Geom.vsub pb pa
176	  let v := Geom.vsub vb va
177	  let vv := Geom.dot v v
178	  if Q.isZero vv then pure none
179	  else
180	    let tstar := Q.neg (Q.div (Geom.dot r v) vv)
181	    if Q.lt tstar Q.zero || Q.gt tstar horizon then pure none
182	    else pure (some (tstar, Geom.norm (Geom.vadd r (Q.mul tstar v.1, Q.mul tstar v.2))))
183	
184	/-- Signed heading change (degrees, left positive) over the back window w, integrated from the yaw
185	    rate; unknown where the window is truncated, sparsely sampled or a yaw rate is missing. -/
186	def prim_heading_change (c : Ctx) (x : TrackId) (w : Q) : Array QR :=
187	  (yawChange c x w).map fun e => match e with
188	    | .error r => .error (match r with
189	        | .windowTruncated _ => .windowTruncated "prim_heading_change"
190	        | .samplingGap _ => .samplingGap "prim_heading_change"
191	        | other => other)
192	    | .ok Δ => .ok Δ
193	
194	/-- The centres approach each other within the horizon. -/
195	def prim_closest_approach_within (c : Ctx) (a b : TrackId) (horizon : Q) : Array R :=
196	  each c fun s => match closestApproach s a b horizon with
197	    | .error w => R.u w
198	    | .ok o => R.ofBool o.isSome

def timePos (c : Ctx) : Array (Option Q) := c.times.map some
def pathPos (c : Ctx) (x : TrackId) : Array (Option Q) := c.scenes.map (kin_path_length · x)
def positions (c : Ctx) (m : Measure) (x : TrackId) : Array (Option Q) :=
  match m with | .time => timePos c | .path => pathPos c x
def missingPos (m : Measure) : UnknownReason :=
  match m with | .time => .outOfRange | .path => .absentAtom "kin_path_length"

def bAtom (o : Option Bool) (name : String) : R := R.ofOption o (.absentAtom name)
def qAtom (o : Option Q) (name : String) : QR :=
  match o with | some q => .ok q | none => .error (.absentAtom name)
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Scene-level helpers over atoms
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
/-- Heading change (degrees, left positive) integrated over the back window of length w:
    prefix sums of yaw rate × interval, one window query per instant. -/
def yawChange (c : Ctx) (x : TrackId) (w : Q) : Array (Except UnknownReason Q) :=
  let n := c.n
  -- sums[i] = Σ_{k ≤ i} ω_k (t_k − t_{k−1}); a missing yaw rate contributes nothing and is tracked
  let sums := (List.range n).foldl (fun (acc : Array Q) i =>
    let prev := if i = 0 then Q.zero else acc[i - 1]!
    let dt := if i = 0 then Q.zero else Q.sub c.times[i]! c.times[i - 1]!
    acc.push (match kin_yaw_rate c.scenes[i]! x with
      | some ω => Q.add prev (Q.mul ω dt)
      | none => prev)) #[]
  -- lastMissing[i] = latest index ≤ i with a missing yaw rate (n when none)
  let lastMissing := (List.range n).foldl (fun (acc : Array Nat) i =>
    acc.push (if (kin_yaw_rate c.scenes[i]! x).isNone then i else (if i = 0 then n else acc[i - 1]!))) #[]
  let wins := Time.backWindows (timePos c) w
  (Array.range n).map fun i =>
    match wins[i]! with
    | none => .error .outOfRange
    | some win =>
      if !win.covered then .error (.windowTruncated "prim_heading_change")
      else if !win.adequate then .error (.samplingGap "prim_heading_change")
      else
        let lm := lastMissing[i]!
        if lm ≠ n && lm > win.j0 then .error (.absentAtom "kin_yaw_rate")
        else .ok (Q.sub sums[i]! sums[win.j0]!)

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- The primitives
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
/-- minute m of the day lies in the window [start, end), wrapping past midnight when end ≤ start. -/
def inWindow (w : TimeWindow) (m : Nat) : Bool :=
  if w.startMinute < w.endMinute then w.startMinute ≤ m && m < w.endMinute
  else m ≥ w.startMinute || m < w.endMinute

private def hasClassOpt (s : Scene) (x : TrackId) (k : RoadUserClass) : Option Bool :=
  (s.user x).bind fun u => if u.unobservedClasses.contains k then none else u.classes.map (·.contains k)

private def vecAtom (o : Option Vec) (name : String) : Except UnknownReason Vec :=
  match o with | some v => .ok v | none => .error (.absentAtom name)

/-- Under constant velocities, the time of closest approach of the two centres and the centre
    distance then; `none` when the paths do not approach within `[0, horizon]`. -/
private def closestApproach (s : Scene) (a b : TrackId) (horizon : Q) : Except UnknownReason (Option (Q × Q)) := do
  let pa ← vecAtom (kin_position s a) "kin_position"
  let pb ← vecAtom (kin_position s b) "kin_position"
  let va ← vecAtom (kin_velocity s a) "kin_velocity"
  let vb ← vecAtom (kin_velocity s b) "kin_velocity"
  let r := Geom.vsub pb pa
  let v := Geom.vsub vb va
  let vv := Geom.dot v v
  if Q.isZero vv then pure none
  else
    let tstar := Q.neg (Q.div (Geom.dot r v) vv)
    if Q.lt tstar Q.zero || Q.gt tstar horizon then pure none
    else pure (some (tstar, Geom.norm (Geom.vadd r (Q.mul tstar v.1, Q.mul tstar v.2))))

/-- Signed heading change (degrees, left positive) over the back window w, integrated from the yaw
    rate; unknown where the window is truncated, sparsely sampled or a yaw rate is missing. -/
def prim_heading_change (c : Ctx) (x : TrackId) (w : Q) : Array QR :=
  (yawChange c x w).map fun e => match e with
    | .error r => .error (match r with
        | .windowTruncated _ => .windowTruncated "prim_heading_change"
        | .samplingGap _ => .samplingGap "prim_heading_change"
        | other => other)
    | .ok Δ => .ok Δ

/-- The centres approach each other within the horizon. -/
def prim_closest_approach_within (c : Ctx) (a b : TrackId) (horizon : Q) : Array R :=
  each c fun s => match closestApproach s a b horizon with
    | .error w => R.u w
    | .ok o => R.ofBool o.isSome

/-
  TrafficSpec.Core.Language.Rule
  What a specification is: binders with class formulas, an applicability and an obligation, and
  the declarations a reviewer needs (parameters, assumptions, declared intentions,
  operationalizations, residues, narrowings, the rules it composes, the surrogate flag).

  A residue is a span of the text the rule does not capture at all; the plan declares it and the
  rule repeats it verbatim. A narrowing is a reading the coder chose on a span the plan does
  carry, stated here so the review judges the rule as it is: the span it names and why. The
  coder may add narrowings and never residues.

  Applicability and obligation are two formulas because a rule whose situation never arises is
  not compliant, it is not engaged: `notApplicable` is a verdict of its own, the witness check can
  demand a scenario for it, and a monitor reads the applicability as the trigger and the
  obligation as what to verify once triggered.

  A surrogate rule (the whole duty is an operationalized standard) is monitored like any other,
  but its verdicts are evidence about the standard, never the law's own verdict; the flag is what
  the monitor and the export propagate so the two are never summed.

  This file holds the declarations only and imports no evaluator: a rule file that imports it
  can state a rule but cannot read a scene, evaluate a formula or build evidence. Evaluation and
  the static check are in RuleEval.lean, which nothing under Rules/ may import.
-/
import TrafficSpec.Core.Language.Formula
import TrafficSpec.Core.Foundations.Unknown

namespace TrafficSpec

/-- A binder: a variable and the class formula (over `ru_*` atoms and class-level derived
    concepts) a track must satisfy to be bound to it. The subject comes first. -/
structure Binder where
  name : String
  cls : Formula
  deriving Repr, Inhabited

/-- A reading chosen on a span the record carries, declared where it is made: the span (a
    segmentation id for a rule, a run of the contract's words for a concept) and what the formulas
    state more narrowly than the words. `kind` is `reading` where the words leave the choice open,
    `observable_reading` where a word with no observable counterpart is read through the conduct
    or the feature it refers to, `no_atom` or `no_operator` where the vocabulary or the language
    cannot state the words — a declaration the gate returns for a gap, never a reading the rule
    stands on. -/
structure Narrowing where
  span : String
  why : String
  kind : String := "reading"
  deriving Repr, Inhabited, DecidableEq

structure Rule where
  id : String                                   -- the node id, derived from the law id
  laws : List String                            -- the corpus ids this rule formalizes
  binders : List Binder
  applicability : Formula
  obligation : Formula
  assumptions : List AsmId := []
  intentions : List IntId := []                 -- the declared intentions its formulas read
  operationalizations : List Operationalization := []
  residues : List String := []                  -- what the text says and the rule does not capture
  narrowings : List Narrowing := []             -- readings the coder chose on carried spans
  surrogate : Bool := false
  deriving Repr, Inhabited

inductive Verdict
  | violated
  | compliant
  | notApplicable
  | unknown (why : List UnknownReason)
  deriving Repr, DecidableEq, Inhabited

namespace Verdict
def tag : Verdict → String
  | .violated => "violated"
  | .compliant => "compliant"
  | .notApplicable => "not_applicable"
  | .unknown _ => "unknown"
def reasons : Verdict → List UnknownReason
  | .unknown w => w
  | _ => []
instance : ToString Verdict := ⟨tag⟩
end Verdict

/-- Kleene combination of the two formulas: not engaged ↦ notApplicable, engaged and the
    obligation decided ↦ compliant/violated, anything undecided ↦ unknown with its reasons. -/
def verdictAt (app obl : R) : Verdict :=
  match app.v with
  | .f => .notApplicable
  | .u => .unknown app.why
  | .t =>
    match obl.v with
    | .t => .compliant
    | .f => .violated
    | .u => .unknown obl.why

theorem verdictAt_notApplicable (app obl : R) (h : app.v = .f) : verdictAt app obl = .notApplicable := by
  unfold verdictAt; rw [h]
theorem verdictAt_violated (app obl : R) (ha : app.v = .t) (ho : obl.v = .f) : verdictAt app obl = .violated := by
  unfold verdictAt; rw [ha, ho]
theorem verdictAt_compliant (app obl : R) (ha : app.v = .t) (ho : obl.v = .t) : verdictAt app obl = .compliant := by
  unfold verdictAt; rw [ha, ho]

namespace Rule
/-- The formulas a rule consists of, class formulas first. -/
def formulas (r : Rule) : List Formula := r.binders.map (·.cls) ++ [r.applicability, r.obligation]
/-- Atom, primitive and concept names the rule reads. -/
def atoms (r : Rule) : List String := (r.formulas.flatMap Formula.atoms).eraseDups
/-- Reading parameters the rule names. -/
def params (r : Rule) : List ParamName := (r.formulas.flatMap Formula.params).eraseDups
/-- Rules the rule composes. -/
def composes (r : Rule) : List String := (r.formulas.flatMap Formula.composed).eraseDups
/-- Assumptions the formulas read. -/
def usedAssumptions (r : Rule) : List AsmId := (r.formulas.flatMap Formula.assumptions).eraseDups
/-- Declared intentions the formulas read. -/
def usedIntentions (r : Rule) : List IntId := (r.formulas.flatMap Formula.intentions).eraseDups
def binderNames (r : Rule) : List String := r.binders.map (·.name)
def subject (r : Rule) : Option String := r.binders.head?.map (·.name)

/-- The rule and, transitively, the rules it composes (each once). -/
def closure (rules : List Rule) (r : Rule) : List Rule :=
  let rec go (fuel : Nat) (seen : List String) (todo : List Rule) : List Rule :=
    match fuel, todo with
    | 0, _ | _, [] => []
    | fuel + 1, x :: rest =>
      let next := x.composes.filterMap fun id =>
        if seen.contains id then none else rules.find? (·.id == id)
      x :: go fuel (seen ++ next.map (·.id)) (rest ++ next)
  go (rules.length + 1) [r.id] [r]

/-- Whether the rule reads a declared intention, in its own formulas or through a rule it
    composes at any depth. -/
def readsIntention (rules : List Rule) (r : Rule) : Bool :=
  (closure rules r).any fun x => !x.usedIntentions.isEmpty
end Rule

end TrafficSpec

/-
  NRS_484B_413_2 — NRS-484B-413-2

  THE READING (the blueprint's; the coding session records here, per span, how each element,
  operationalization and composition below is written, and every choice the text did not dictate).

  Spans:
    s1 (obligation): A signal of intention to turn right or left, or otherwise turn a vehicle from a direct course, shall be given continuously during not less than the last 100 feet traveled
    s2 (condition): in a business or residential district and not less than the last 300 feet traveled in any other area
    s3 (condition): prior to changing the course of a vehicle.
    s4 (condition): This rule shall be observed, regardless of the weather.

  Elements (span → atoms, derived):
    s1: atoms ['kin.path_length', 'kin.yaw_rate', 'ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle', 'sig.hand_signal', 'sig.turn_indicator'], derived []
    s3: atoms [], derived ['drv.motion.turning']

  Literals the text states (each written through its Units constructor):
    s1: 100 ft — 100 feet
    s2: 300 ft — 300 feet

  No magnitude below is this file's own: parameters name the reading, literals are the text's.

  How each span is written:

  - binder `v` (subject): `ru_aggregate v "DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"` — the admitted aggregate id,
    never the classes the posted definition covers.

  - s3 (condition, the occasion of the duty): `drv.motion.turning` rises for `v`
    (`.rises (.derived "drv_motion_turning" [v] [p.turn_recognition_window,
    p.heading_change_noise_floor])`). The concept is the law's own "turn right or left, or
    otherwise turn ... from a direct course"; "prior to" is read, as the record states, from the
    observation at which that change is first recognized, and the window of travelled path runs
    back from it. The parameters are the node's, in the concept's order (window, tolerance).

  - s1 + s2 (the duty and the length it selects): over the window of path travelled behind that
    observation — `.holdsFor .path (100 ft) "v"` where the trace declares
    `asm.in_business_or_residential_district`, `.holdsFor .path (300 ft) "v"` where it declares it
    does not — `v` gave the signal of the hand of the course change at every observation:
    `sig_turn_indicator v <hand>` or `sig_hand_signal v <hand>`. The two lengths are written as a
    pair of conditionals on the declaration rather than a `cond` term, because a window's length
    must be a constant term (`Rule.check`); where the trace declares the district neither way both
    conditionals are undecided and the verdict is unknown, as the record requires. The hand is
    read at the judged observation from the sign of `kin.yaw_rate` (left positive), outside the
    window, so that the window asks for the hand of the course change being judged and not for the
    hand of each past observation.

  - s4: residue, as the plan declares it; no weather atom is read.

  Narrowing declared by this session (the record's own narrowings are not restated): the hand is
  read from the SIGN of `kin.yaw_rate`, so at an observation whose rate of change of heading is
  exactly zero neither hand is read and the duty is not stated there — see `narrowings` below.
-/
import TrafficSpec.Core.Language.Rule

namespace TrafficSpec.Rules.NRS_484B_413_2

/-- The binders, as arguments (order and names are the node's). -/
def vV : Arg := .var "v"

/-- The reading's parameters; no value of any of them lives in this file. -/
def pHeadingChangeNoiseFloor : Term := .param "p.heading_change_noise_floor"
def pTurnRecognitionWindow : Term := .param "p.turn_recognition_window"

def zeroMetres : Term := .lit Q.zero .metre

/-- The district declaration of s2, which selects the length of the window. -/
def inDistrict : Formula := .asm "asm.in_business_or_residential_district"

/-- The text's own figures (s1, s2), each through the `Units` constructor of its unit. -/
def feet100 : Term := .lit (Units.feet 100) .metre
def feet300 : Term := .lit (Units.feet 300) .metre

/-- The subject's rate of change of heading at the judged observation, left positive. -/
def yawRateOfV : Term := .measure "kin_yaw_rate" [vV]
def zeroYawRate : Term := .lit Q.zero .degreePerSecond

/-- Class of `v`: ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle -/
def clsV : Formula := .atom "ru_aggregate" [vV, .lit "DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"] []

/-- s3: the subject's heading is changing at the observation — the concept of the node's element,
    with the node's parameters in the concept's order. -/
def turning : Formula :=
  .derived "drv_motion_turning" [vV] [pTurnRecognitionWindow, pHeadingChangeNoiseFloor]

/-- Applicability: s2 (condition): in a business or residential district and not less than the last 300 feet traveled in any other area; s3 (condition): prior to changing the course of a vehicle.; s4 (condition): This rule shall be observed, regardless of the weather. -/
def applicability : Formula := .rises turning

/-- The signal of the hand `h`: the indicator lit on that hand, or an arm signal whose meaning is
    that hand. -/
def signalOfHand (h : String) : Formula :=
  .or (.atom "sig_turn_indicator" [vV, .lit h] [])
      (.atom "sig_hand_signal" [vV, .lit h] [])

/-- The signal of the hand of the course change at every observation of the window of travelled
    path `d` behind the judged observation; the hand is read here, at that observation. -/
def gaveSignalOver (d : Term) : Formula :=
  .and
    (.implies (.cmp yawRateOfV .gt zeroYawRate) (.holdsFor .path d "v" (signalOfHand "left")))
    (.implies (.cmp yawRateOfV .lt zeroYawRate) (.holdsFor .path d "v" (signalOfHand "right")))

/-- Obligation: s1 (obligation): A signal of intention to turn right or left, or otherwise turn a vehicle from a direct course, shall be given continuously during not less than the last 100 feet traveled -/
def obligation : Formula :=
  .and
    (.implies inDistrict (gaveSignalOver feet100))
    (.implies (.not inDistrict) (gaveSignalOver feet300))

def rule : Rule :=
  { id := "NRS_484B_413_2"
    laws := ["NRS-484B-413-2"]
    binders :=
      [ { name := "v", cls := clsV } ]
    applicability := applicability
    obligation := obligation
    assumptions := ["asm.in_business_or_residential_district"]
    intentions := []
    operationalizations := []
    residues := ["The words add no observable condition and no restriction: the signal is owed over the same window, in the same terms, whether or not rain, snow, wet road, ice or any other weather is present, so the duty is the same whether or not these words hold. The rule reads no weather atom for them, and nothing of the obligation is dropped."]  -- the node's, verbatim; not yours to change
    narrowings :=
      [ { span := "s1"
          why := "The hand of the course change is read from the sign of kin.yaw_rate at the judged observation: strictly positive is left, strictly negative is right. At an observation whose rate of change of heading is exactly zero no hand is read, so the duty of s1 is stated for a course change whose rate of change of heading is non-zero where it is recognized; the signal is required on the hand the sign gives and a signal on the other hand does not satisfy it."
          kind := "reading" } ]
    surrogate := false }

end TrafficSpec.Rules.NRS_484B_413_2

/-

  The geometry, once, for every scenario below (every figure here is the witness's own and appears
  nowhere in the rule):

  - One straight two-way-less carriageway: a single lane, 4 m wide, running east from x = -20 m to
    x = 200 m, centred on y = 0.
  - One road user, track 1, a motor vehicle (half extents 2 m × 1 m × 1 m), the subject of every
    scene, grounded to the binder `v`. No other road user is ever present.
  - 30 observations, 0.5 s apart (t = 0 … 14 500 ms). The subject runs east along the centre of the
    lane at 10 m/s, so each observation is 5 m of travelled path further on: `kin.path_length` is
    5 k metres at observation k, and the subject's position is (5 k, 0).
  - The course change is carried by the atom the duty and the concept read, `kin.yaw_rate`: it is
    zero at observations 0 … 24 and ±20 deg/s from observation 25 on (positive to the left).
    Integrated over the recognition window behind an observation (the reading's 3 s), that is 0 deg
    at observation 24 and 10 deg at observation 25 — well below and well above the reading's 5 deg
    noise floor — so `drv.motion.turning` rises at observation 25 (t = 12 500 ms) and nowhere else,
    and observation 25 is the judged one.
  - The windows of travelled path behind observation 25 are therefore: 100 ft = 30.48 m reaching
    back to observation 19 (125 m − 95 m = 30 m), and 300 ft = 91.44 m reaching back to
    observation 7 (125 m − 35 m = 90 m). Both are covered by observed instants and sampled 5 m
    apart, a quarter of the shorter window.
  - Each scenario declares `asm.in_business_or_residential_district` true or false in every scene,
    and every scenario names the instants it speaks about (`window` = 10 000 … 14 000 ms, i.e.
    observations 20 … 28), because the recognition window and the path windows are truncated at the
    start of any finite trace.

  The signal is stated by `sig.turn_indicator` and `sig.hand_signal` on the subject, per
  observation; the scenarios differ only in the district declaration, the hand of the bend and
  those two signals.
-/

import TrafficSpec.Core.Evidence.Builders

namespace TrafficSpecWitness.NRS_484B_413_2

open TrafficSpec

def m (n : Int) : Q := Units.metres n
def cm (n : Int) : Q := Units.centimetres n

def dtS : Q := Units.milliseconds 500
def nScenes : Nat := 30
/-- The observation at which the bend begins, and the one at which it is recognized. -/
def bend : Nat := 25
/-- 10 m/s, so 5 m of travelled path per observation. -/
def speedV : Q := Units.metresPerSecond 10
def stepM : Q := m 5
def halfExtent : Q × Q × Q := (m 2, m 1, m 1)
/-- A bend to the left and a bend to the right, in degrees per second (left positive). -/
def yawLeft : Q := Units.degrees 20
def yawRight : Q := Units.degrees (-20)

/-- The lane the subject runs along. -/
def laneRegion : Structure :=
  Build.lane 10 [(m (-20), m (-2)), (m 200, m (-2)), (m 200, m 2), (m (-20), m 2)] Build.east

+def yawRight : Q := Units.degrees (-20)

+    (Build.withSignals
+      (Build.user 1 [.motorVehicle] (along, Q.zero) Build.east speedV halfExtent (some along))
+      (fun s => { s with turnIndicator := some ind, handSignal := some hand }))

/-
  TrafficSpec.Core.Runtime.Monitor
  The report: one row per rule and grounding, with support, episode verdict, timeline, the
  histogram of unknown reasons, residues and the surrogate flag; rendered as tab-separated text
  (the gate's contract) and as JSON lines (the diagnosis tooling's).

  It composes everything below it and owns nothing else. The row format is a contract with
  `tools/check_spec.py` and `scripts/diagnostics/`; changing a line here is a cross-artifact change.
  Surrogate rows never enter the concrete tallies.

  Text format (tab-separated; one record per line):
    SOURCE   source  instants=N  gap=<seconds>
    RULE     rule  concrete|surrogate  support  absent-ids(,)  groundings=N  live=bool  v=N c=N na=N u=N
    GROUND   rule  grounding  episode
    TL       rule  grounding  t_from  t_to  verdict            (runs of equal verdict, ms timestamps)
    UNK      rule  grounding  reason  count
    RESIDUE  rule  text
    SUMMARY  concrete|surrogate  rules=N supported=N partial=N unsupported=N live=N v=N c=N na=N u=N
-/
import Lean.Data.Json
import TrafficSpec.Core.Runtime.Grounding
import TrafficSpec.Core.Runtime.Manifest

namespace TrafficSpec
namespace Monitor
open Grounding

structure Row where
  rule : String
  surrogate : Bool
  support : Support
  grounding : Grounding
  episode : Verdict
  timeline : Array (Timestamp × Verdict)
  unknowns : List (String × Nat)
  residues : List String
  deriving Repr, Inhabited

structure RuleLine where
  rule : String
  surrogate : Bool
  support : Support
  groundings : Nat
  live : Bool
  violated : Nat
  compliant : Nat
  notApplicable : Nat
  unknown : Nat
  deriving Repr, Inhabited

structure Report where
  source : String
  instants : Nat
  gap : Q
  rules : List RuleLine
  rows : List Row
  deriving Repr, Inhabited

def histogram (tl : List Verdict) : List (String × Nat) :=
  let tags := tl.flatMap fun v => (v.reasons.map UnknownReason.tag).eraseDups
  tags.eraseDups.map fun t => (t, tags.count t)

def countVerdict (vs : List Verdict) (p : Verdict → Bool) : Nat := (vs.filter p).length
def isUnknown : Verdict → Bool | .unknown _ => true | _ => false

/-- Evaluate a rule set over one trace as the source would have produced it, the rules' concept
    calls expanded over `cs`. Unsupported rules are reported without groundings: nothing they
    say could be decided. A trace the admission rejects is not evaluated: its defects are returned. -/
def check (rules : List Rule) (τ : Trace) (ρ : Reading) (m : Manifest) (cs : List Concept := []) : Except (List String) Report := do
  let rules := rules.map (Concept.expandRule cs)
  let S ← Setup.admit rules (maskTrace m τ) ρ m.reidGap
  let per := rules.map fun r =>
    let sup := support rules r m
    match sup with
    | .unsupported _ => ({ rule := r.id, surrogate := r.surrogate, support := sup, groundings := 0, live := false,
                           violated := 0, compliant := 0, notApplicable := 0, unknown := 0 : RuleLine }, ([] : List Row))
    | _ =>
      let evaluated : List (Grounding × Grounding.Timeline × Verdict) := Grounding.check S r
      let rows : List Row := evaluated.map fun (e : Grounding × Grounding.Timeline × Verdict) =>
        let g := e.1; let tl := e.2.1; let ep := e.2.2
        let vs : List Verdict := tl.verdicts.toList.map Prod.snd
        { rule := r.id, surrogate := r.surrogate, support := sup, grounding := g, episode := ep,
          timeline := tl.verdicts, unknowns := histogram vs, residues := r.residues }
      let eps : List Verdict := rows.map Row.episode
      ({ rule := r.id, surrogate := r.surrogate, support := sup, groundings := rows.length,
         live := evaluated.any (fun e => e.2.1.live),
         violated := countVerdict eps (· == Verdict.violated), compliant := countVerdict eps (· == Verdict.compliant),
         notApplicable := countVerdict eps (· == Verdict.notApplicable), unknown := countVerdict eps isUnknown : RuleLine }, rows)
  pure { source := m.source, instants := τ.length, gap := m.reidGap, rules := per.map (·.1), rows := per.flatMap (·.2) }

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Text
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
def qText (q : Q) : String :=
  let g := Nat.gcd q.num.natAbs q.den
  let g := if g == 0 then 1 else g
  let n := q.num / (Int.ofNat g)
  let d := q.den / g
  if d == 1 then toString n else s!"{n}/{d}"
def tabs (xs : List String) : String := String.intercalate "\t" xs
def kind (surrogate : Bool) : String := if surrogate then "surrogate" else "concrete"

/-- Runs of equal verdicts: (from, to, verdict). -/
def runs (tl : Array (Timestamp × Verdict)) : List (Timestamp × Timestamp × Verdict) :=
  tl.toList.foldl (fun acc (t, v) =>
    match acc with
    | (a, _, v') :: rest => if v' == v then (a, t, v) :: rest else (t, t, v) :: acc
    | [] => [(t, t, v)]) [] |>.reverse

def rowLines (row : Row) : List String :=
  let g := row.grounding.render
  [tabs ["GROUND", row.rule, g, row.episode.tag]] ++
  ((runs row.timeline).map fun (a, b', v) => tabs ["TL", row.rule, g, toString a, toString b', v.tag]) ++
  (row.unknowns.map fun (t, n) => tabs ["UNK", row.rule, g, t, toString n])

def ruleLine (l : RuleLine) : String :=
  tabs ["RULE", l.rule, kind l.surrogate, l.support.tag, String.intercalate "," l.support.absent,
        s!"groundings={l.groundings}", s!"live={l.live}",
        s!"v={l.violated}", s!"c={l.compliant}", s!"na={l.notApplicable}", s!"u={l.unknown}"]

def summaryLine (surrogate : Bool) (ls : List RuleLine) : String :=
  let ls := ls.filter (·.surrogate == surrogate)
  let n (p : RuleLine → Bool) := (ls.filter p).length
  let sum (f : RuleLine → Nat) := ls.foldl (fun a l => a + f l) 0
  tabs ["SUMMARY", kind surrogate, s!"rules={ls.length}",
        s!"supported={n (·.support == .supported)}",
        s!"partial={n fun l => match l.support with | .partially _ => true | _ => false}",
        s!"unsupported={n fun l => match l.support with | .unsupported _ => true | _ => false}",
        s!"live={n (·.live)}", s!"v={sum (·.violated)}", s!"c={sum (·.compliant)}",
        s!"na={sum (·.notApplicable)}", s!"u={sum (·.unknown)}"]

def renderText (rep : Report) : String :=
  let header := tabs ["SOURCE", rep.source, s!"instants={rep.instants}", s!"gap={qText rep.gap}"]
  let ruleBlocks := rep.rules.flatMap fun l =>
    let residues : List String := ((rep.rows.find? (·.rule == l.rule)).map (·.residues)).getD []
    [ruleLine l] ++
    (rep.rows.filter (·.rule == l.rule)).flatMap rowLines ++
    residues.map fun t => tabs ["RESIDUE", l.rule, t]
  String.intercalate "\n" ([header] ++ ruleBlocks ++ [summaryLine false rep.rules, summaryLine true rep.rules]) ++ "\n"

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- JSON lines
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
open Lean in
def verdictJson (v : Verdict) : Json :=
  Json.mkObj [("verdict", v.tag), ("reasons", Json.arr (v.reasons.map fun r => Json.str r.tag).toArray)]

open Lean in
def rowJson (row : Row) : Json :=
  Json.mkObj [
    ("kind", "grounding"), ("rule", row.rule), ("surrogate", row.surrogate), ("support", row.support.tag),
    ("grounding", Json.mkObj (row.grounding.assign.map fun (n, t) => (n, Json.num t))),
    ("episode", verdictJson row.episode),
    ("timeline", Json.arr ((runs row.timeline).map fun (a, b', v) =>
        Json.mkObj [("from", Json.num a), ("to", Json.num b'), ("verdict", v.tag)]).toArray),
    ("unknowns", Json.mkObj (row.unknowns.map fun (t, n) => (t, Json.num n))),
    ("residues", Json.arr (row.residues.map Json.str).toArray)]

open Lean in
def ruleJson (l : RuleLine) : Json :=
  Json.mkObj [
    ("kind", "rule"), ("rule", l.rule), ("surrogate", l.surrogate), ("support", l.support.tag),
    ("absent", Json.arr (l.support.absent.map Json.str).toArray), ("groundings", Json.num l.groundings),
    ("live", l.live), ("violated", Json.num l.violated), ("compliant", Json.num l.compliant),
    ("not_applicable", Json.num l.notApplicable), ("unknown", Json.num l.unknown)]

open Lean in
def renderJsonLines (rep : Report) : String :=
  let header := Json.mkObj [("kind", "source"), ("source", rep.source), ("instants", Json.num rep.instants), ("gap", qText rep.gap)]
  String.intercalate "\n" ((header :: rep.rules.map ruleJson ++ rep.rows.map rowJson).map (·.compress)) ++ "\n"

end Monitor
end TrafficSpec

/-
  Witnesses for NRS_484B_413_2.

  The geometry, once, for every scenario below (every figure here is the witness's own and appears
  nowhere in the rule):

  - One straight lane, 4 m wide, running east from x = -20 m to x = 200 m, centred on y = 0.
  - One road user, track 1, a motor vehicle (half extents 2 m x 1 m x 1 m), the subject of every
    scene and the track the binder `v` is grounded to. No other road user is ever present.
  - 26 observations, 0.5 s apart (t = 0 ... 12 500 ms). The subject runs at 10 m/s, so each
    observation is 5 m of travelled path further on: at observation k < 25 it is at (5 k, 0),
    heading due east, with a zero yaw rate, and `kin.path_length` is 5 k metres.
  - The course change is one observation long and it is carried by the atom the duty and the
    concept read, `kin.yaw_rate`: at observation 25 the rate is +-20 deg/s (positive to the left),
    so over the half second behind it the heading turns by 10 deg. The scene states that turn:
    the heading at observation 25 is east rotated by +-10 deg (cos 10, +- sin 10, to nine decimals)
    and the position is the previous one advanced 5 m along that heading, (124.924, +- 0.868),
    with `kin.path_length` 125 m.
  - Integrated over the recognition window behind an observation (the reading's 3 s), the heading
    change is 0 deg at observation 24 and 10 deg at observation 25 -- well below and well above the
    reading's 5 deg noise floor -- so `drv.motion.turning` rises at observation 25 (t = 12 500 ms)
    and nowhere else: observation 25 is the judged one.
  - The windows of travelled path behind observation 25 are therefore: 100 ft = 30.48 m reaching
    back to observation 19 (125 m - 95 m = 30 m), and 300 ft = 91.44 m reaching back to
    observation 7 (125 m - 35 m = 90 m). Both are covered by observed instants and sampled 5 m
    apart, a sixth of the shorter window.
  - Each scenario declares `asm.in_business_or_residential_district` true or false in every scene,
    and every scenario names the instants it speaks about (`window` = 10 000 ... 12 500 ms, i.e.
    observations 20 ... 25), because the recognition window and the windows of travelled path are
    truncated at the start of any finite trace.

  The signal is stated by `sig.turn_indicator` and `sig.hand_signal` on the subject at every
  observation; the scenarios differ only in the district declaration, the hand of the bend and
  those two signals.
-/
import TrafficSpec.Rules.NRS_484B.NRS_484B_413_2
import TrafficSpec.Core.Evidence.Builders

namespace TrafficSpecWitness.NRS_484B_413_2

open TrafficSpec

def m (n : Int) : Q := Units.metres n
def cm (n : Int) : Q := Units.centimetres n

/-- Observations 0.5 s apart; twenty-six of them. -/
def dtS : Q := Units.milliseconds 500
def nScenes : Nat := 26
/-- The one observation at which the heading turns, and at which the turn is recognized. -/
def bend : Nat := 25
/-- 10 m/s, so 5 m of travelled path per observation. -/
def speedV : Q := Units.metresPerSecond 10
def stepM : Q := m 5
def halfExtent : Q × Q × Q := (m 2, m 1, m 1)
/-- A bend to the left and a bend to the right, in degrees per second (left positive): over the
    half second behind the bend observation, 10 degrees either way. -/
def yawLeft : Q := Units.degrees 20
def yawRight : Q := Units.degrees (-20)

/-- East rotated by ten degrees, to nine decimals. -/
def cos10 : Q := Units.ratio 984807753 1000000000
def sin10 : Q := Units.ratio 173648178 1000000000
def headingLeft : Vec := (cos10, sin10)
def headingRight : Vec := (cos10, Units.ratio (-173648178) 1000000000)
/-- The previous position (120, 0) advanced 5 m along that heading. -/
def bendPosLeft : Vec := (Units.micrometres 124924039, Units.micrometres 868241)
def bendPosRight : Vec := (Units.micrometres 124924039, Units.micrometres (-868241))

/-- The lane the subject runs along. -/
def laneRegion : Structure :=
  Build.lane 10 [(m (-20), m (-2)), (m 200, m (-2)), (m 200, m 2), (m (-20), m 2)] Build.east

/-- The subject at observation `k`: 5 m of path further on, with the yaw rate and the two signals
    given. Where the yaw rate is zero it runs due east along the centre of the lane; where it is
    not, the heading and the position are the turn that rate carries over the half second behind. -/
def subjectAt (k : Nat) (yaw : Q) (ind : TurnIndicatorState) (hand : HandSignal) : RoadUser :=
  let along := Q.mul (Q.ofInt (Int.ofNat k)) stepM
  let left := Q.lt Q.zero yaw
  let pos : Vec := if Q.isZero yaw then (along, Q.zero) else if left then bendPosLeft else bendPosRight
  let head : Vec := if Q.isZero yaw then Build.east else if left then headingLeft else headingRight
  Build.withKin
    (Build.withSignals
      (Build.user 1 [.motorVehicle] pos head speedV halfExtent (some along))
      (fun s => { s with turnIndicator := some ind, handSignal := some hand }))
    (fun kin => { kin with yawRate := some yaw })

def sceneAt (k : Nat) (t : Timestamp) (district : Bool) (yaw : Q)
    (ind : TurnIndicatorState) (hand : HandSignal) : Scene :=
  Build.scene t (some 1) [subjectAt k yaw ind hand] [laneRegion] []
    (assumptions := [("asm.in_business_or_residential_district", district)])

/-- A whole recording: the district declaration, the hand of the bend at observation `bend`, and
    the indicator state and the arm signal per observation. -/
def runTrace (district : Bool) (yawAtBend : Q)
    (indAt : Nat → TurnIndicatorState) (handAt : Nat → HandSignal) : Trace :=
  Build.trace nScenes 0 dtS fun k t =>
    sceneAt k t district (if k < bend then Q.zero else yawAtBend) (indAt k) (handAt k)

def noIndicator (_ : Nat) : TurnIndicatorState := .off
def indicatorAlways (s : TurnIndicatorState) : Nat → TurnIndicatorState := fun _ => s
/-- The indicator lit from observation `k0` on, and off before it. -/
def indicatorFrom (s : TurnIndicatorState) (k0 : Nat) : Nat → TurnIndicatorState :=
  fun k => if k0 ≤ k then s else .off
def noArm (_ : Nat) : HandSignal := .noSignal
def armAlways (h : HandSignal) : Nat → HandSignal := fun _ => h

/-- `forbid` (violated): The trace declares the stretch the subject occupies to lie in a business district. The subject runs straight, then bends to the right until its heading change over the recognition window reaches the noise floor; over the whole hundred feet of path travelled before that observation its indicator was off and no arm signal was given. -/

    scene, grounded to the binder `v`. No other road user is ever present.
  - 30 observations, 0.5 s apart (t = 0 … 14 500 ms). The subject runs east along the centre of the
    lane at 10 m/s, so each observation is 5 m of travelled path further on: `kin.path_length` is
    5 k metres at observation k, and the subject's position is (5 k, 0).
  - The course change is carried by the atom the duty and the concept read, `kin.yaw_rate`: it is
    zero at observations 0 … 24 and ±20 deg/s from observation 25 on (positive to the left).
    Integrated over the recognition window behind an observation (the reading's 3 s), that is 0 deg
    at observation 24 and 10 deg at observation 25 — well below and well above the reading's 5 deg
    noise floor — so `drv.motion.turning` rises at observation 25 (t = 12 500 ms) and nowhere else,
    and observation 25 is the judged one.
  - The windows of travelled path behind observation 25 are therefore: 100 ft = 30.48 m reaching
    back to observation 19 (125 m − 95 m = 30 m), and 300 ft = 91.44 m reaching back to
    observation 7 (125 m − 35 m = 90 m). Both are covered by observed instants and sampled 5 m
    apart, a quarter of the shorter window.
  - Each scenario declares `asm.in_business_or_residential_district` true or false in every scene,
    and every scenario names the instants it speaks about (`window` = 10 000 … 14 000 ms, i.e.
    observations 20 … 28), because the recognition window and the path windows are truncated at the
    start of any finite trace.

  The signal is stated by `sig.turn_indicator` and `sig.hand_signal` on the subject, per
  observation; the scenarios differ only in the district declaration, the hand of the bend and
  those two signals.
-/

import TrafficSpec.Core.Evidence.Builders

namespace TrafficSpecWitness.NRS_484B_413_2

open TrafficSpec

def m (n : Int) : Q := Units.metres n
def cm (n : Int) : Q := Units.centimetres n

/-- Observations 0.5 s apart; thirty of them. -/
def dtS : Q := Units.milliseconds 500
def nScenes : Nat := 30
/-- The observation at which the bend begins, and the one at which it is recognized. -/
def bend : Nat := 25
/-- 10 m/s, so 5 m of travelled path per observation. -/
def speedV : Q := Units.metresPerSecond 10
def stepM : Q := m 5
def halfExtent : Q × Q × Q := (m 2, m 1, m 1)
/-- A bend to the left and a bend to the right, in degrees per second (left positive). -/
def yawLeft : Q := Units.degrees 20
def yawRight : Q := Units.degrees (-20)

/-- The lane the subject runs along. -/
def laneRegion : Structure :=
  Build.lane 10 [(m (-20), m (-2)), (m 200, m (-2)), (m 200, m 2), (m (-20), m 2)] Build.east

/-- The subject at observation `k`: 5 m further on, with the yaw rate and the two signals given. -/

  let along := Q.mul (Q.ofInt (Int.ofNat k)) stepM

    (Build.withSignals
      (Build.user 1 [.motorVehicle] (along, Q.zero) Build.east speedV halfExtent (some along))

    (fun kin => { kin with yawRate := some yaw })

    (ind : TurnIndicatorState) (hand : HandSignal) : Scene :=

    (assumptions := [("asm.in_business_or_residential_district", district)])

    and the indicator state and arm signal per observation. -/

    sceneAt k t district (if k < bend then Q.zero else yawAfter) (indAt k) (handAt k)

def indicatorAlways (s : TurnIndicatorState) : Nat → TurnIndicatorState := fun _ => s

def permitTrace : Trace := runTrace false yawLeft (indicatorAlways .left) noArm

/-- `idle` (not_applicable): The subject runs along its lane for the whole recording, its heading change over the recognition window never reaching the noise floor, so no course change is recognized and no signal is owed. -/
def idleTrace : Trace := runTrace false Q.zero noIndicator noArm

def blindTrace : Trace := runTrace true yawLeft (indicatorAlways .left) (armAlways .left)

def branch_1Trace : Trace := runTrace false yawLeft (indicatorAlways .right) noArm

/-- `branch_2` (compliant): In a declared business district, the subject gives no indicator but the driver holds out an arm whose signal means left at every observation of the hundred feet of travelled path before its heading change to the left is recognized. -/
def branch_2Trace : Trace := runTrace true yawLeft noIndicator (armAlways .left)

/-- `branch_3` (violated): Outside any district by the declaration, the subject bends to the right
    with neither indicator nor arm signal over the three hundred feet behind the recognition. -/
def branch_3Trace : Trace := runTrace false yawRight noIndicator noArm

/-- `branch_4` (violated): In a declared district, the subject bends to the left with neither
    indicator nor arm signal over the hundred feet behind the recognition. -/
def branch_4Trace : Trace := runTrace true yawLeft noIndicator noArm

/-- `branch_5` (compliant): In a declared district, the left indicator is lit only from observation
    15 (75 m of travelled path) on — the last 50 m, more than the hundred feet owed in a district
    and less than the three hundred feet owed outside one — before the left bend is recognized. -/
def branch_5Trace : Trace := runTrace true yawLeft (indicatorFrom .left 15) noArm

/-- `branch_6` (violated): the same recording outside any district, where three hundred feet of
    signal are owed and only the last fifty metres were given. -/
def branch_6Trace : Trace := runTrace false yawLeft (indicatorFrom .left 15) noArm

/-- `branch_7` (compliant): Outside any district, the right indicator is lit over the whole
    recording and the subject bends to the right. -/
def branch_7Trace : Trace := runTrace false yawRight (indicatorAlways .right) noArm

/-- `branch_8` (compliant): In a declared district, the driver's arm signal means right at every
    observation of the hundred feet behind a recognized bend to the right. -/
def branch_8Trace : Trace := runTrace true yawRight noIndicator (armAlways .right)

def witness (name : String) (τ : Trace) (expected : Verdict)
    (absent : List String := []) (boundary : String := "") : Scenario :=
  { name := name
    rule := "NRS_484B_413_2"
    trace := τ
    reading := {}          -- ignored by the gate: the run's reading is substituted
    manifest := Build.manifest absent
    grounding := [("v", 1)]
    expected := expected
    -- observations 20 … 28: the recognition window and the path windows are covered there
    window := some (10000, 14000)
    boundary := boundary }

def scenarios : List Scenario :=
  [ witness "forbid" forbidTrace .violated
  , witness "permit" permitTrace .compliant
  , witness "idle" idleTrace .notApplicable
  , witness "blind" blindTrace (.unknown []) ["sig.turn_indicator", "sig.hand_signal"]
  , witness "branch_1" branch_1Trace .violated
  , witness "branch_2" branch_2Trace .compliant
  , witness "branch_3" branch_3Trace .violated
  , witness "branch_4" branch_4Trace .violated
  , witness "branch_5" branch_5Trace .compliant
  , witness "branch_6" branch_6Trace .violated
  , witness "branch_7" branch_7Trace .compliant
  , witness "branch_8" branch_8Trace .compliant ]

end TrafficSpecWitness.NRS_484B_413_2

# NRS_484B_413_2 — coding session result

**Final verdict: `OK`** (3 gate runs of 6 used; 12 witnesses, 6 planned names, composes nothing,
1 coder narrowing).

## The rule, span by span

- **binder `v`** — `ru_aggregate v "DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"`: the admitted aggregate id, not the
  classes the posted definition covers.
- **s3 (the occasion)** — `applicability := .rises (.derived "drv_motion_turning" [v]
  [p.turn_recognition_window, p.heading_change_noise_floor])`. The concept is the node's element for
  "changing the course of a vehicle"; "prior to" is read, as the record states, from the observation
  at which that change is first recognized. Parameters in the catalogue's order (window, tolerance).
- **s1 + s2 (the duty and the length s2 selects)** —
  `and (asm → gaveSignalOver 100 ft) (¬asm → gaveSignalOver 300 ft)`, where
  `gaveSignalOver d = and (yaw_rate > 0 → holdsFor .path d "v" (ind left ∨ arm left))
  (yaw_rate < 0 → holdsFor .path d "v" (ind right ∨ arm right))`.
  The hand is read at the judged observation from the sign of `kin.yaw_rate` (left positive),
  *outside* the window, so the window asks for the hand of the course change being judged and not
  for a hand read at each past observation. `kin.path_length` is read as the measure of the
  `.path` windows, as the element's justification states.
- **s4** — residue, verbatim from the node; no weather atom is read.

## Choices the node left open

1. **Two conditionals instead of one `cond` length.** The record says the length is "selected by a
   condition on that declaration". A window's length must be a *constant* term
   (`Rule.check`/`Term.isConstant` excludes `.cond`), so the selection is written as
   `asm → (100 ft duty)` conjoined with `¬asm → (300 ft duty)`. This preserves the record's
   three-valued requirement: where the trace declares the district neither way both conditionals are
   undecided and the verdict is unknown.
2. **The hand at a zero yaw rate** — declared as the session's one narrowing on s1 (an obligation
   span): the hand is read from the *sign* of `kin.yaw_rate`, so at an observation whose rate of
   change of heading is exactly zero neither hand is read and the duty is not stated there. A signal
   on the other hand does not satisfy the duty, as the record's own narrowing requires.
   No other narrowing is declared; the record's own narrowings are not restated.

## Witnesses

All twelve share one geometry (documented in the witness header): one lane, one motor vehicle
(track 1 ↦ `v`), 26 observations 0.5 s apart, 10 m/s, 5 m of travelled path per observation. The
course change is one observation long and is carried by `kin.yaw_rate` = ±32.52 deg/s at
observation 25, with the heading there the exact unit vector (24/25, ±7/25) and the position the
previous one advanced exactly 5 m along it — so `drv.motion.turning` rises at observation 25
(16.26 deg of heading change against the reading's 5 deg floor) and nowhere else. Every scenario
names `window = 10 000 … 12 500 ms` (observations 20 … 25), because the recognition window and the
windows of travelled path are truncated at the start of any finite trace; no witness is unknown for
truncation.

Beyond the six planned names, six `branch_<n>` witnesses exercise the leaves the planned scenes do
not reach: the duty has four combinations (district / no district × left / right hand) and two
alternative signals in each, so each combination needs a scene in which both alternatives are false
and one in which the district declaration decides the length:

| witness | district | hand | signal | expected |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `forbid` | yes | right | none | violated |
| `permit` | no | left | left indicator throughout (410 ft) | compliant |
| `idle` | no | — (straight) | none | not_applicable |
| `blind` | yes | left | both signal atoms masked | unknown |
| `branch_1` | no | left | right indicator throughout | violated |
| `branch_2` | yes | left | arm signal left throughout | compliant |
| `branch_3` | no | right | none | violated |
| `branch_4` | yes | left | none | violated |
| `branch_5` | yes | left | left indicator over the last 50 m (164 ft) | compliant |
| `branch_6` | no | left | left indicator over the last 50 m | violated |
| `branch_7` | no | right | right indicator throughout | compliant |
| `branch_8` | yes | right | arm signal right throughout | compliant |

`branch_5`/`branch_6` are the pair that makes the district declaration itself decisive: the same
50 m of signal keeps the 100 ft bound in a district and breaks the 300 ft bound outside one, each by
a clear margin (164 ft > 100 ft, 164 ft < 300 ft).

## Gate runs

1. **`WITNESS_FAIL`** — "its trace is not one the adapter can produce: track 1 keeps the heading it
   had at t=…, but its yaw rate turns it -10° over the interval (the rate at a scene is held over
   the interval before it)". The first traces stated the bend through the yaw rate alone and kept
   the subject on a straight line heading east. *Changed:* the bend was reduced to a single
   observation and the scene now states the turn it carries — the heading rotated by the yaw rate
   over the half second behind, the position advanced along that heading.
2. **`WITNESS_FAIL`** — "path_length grows by 5 m since t=12000, less than the straight-line
   distance between its two positions": the micrometre rounding of a 10° rotation pushed the chord
   1.6 µm past 5 m. *Changed:* the turn now uses the exactly representable unit heading
   (24/25, 7/25) with the yaw rate `Units.millidegrees 32520`, so the chord, the position, the
   velocity and the path increment are exact (5 m) and only the yaw rate carries a rounding of
   0.0002°.
3. **`OK`**.

## Why I finished

The gate returned `OK`: the rule builds, checks, declares what the node declares, uses every
claimed name and no other, carries no bare literal, and all twelve witnesses reach their expected
verdicts — the four planned ones for the reasons the plan names (the `blind` witness unknown only
for the two atoms its manifest masks). The node needed no repair: every span it carries is written
with the atoms and the concept it claims, and nothing in it had to be read against its words.

What I wrote:

- **Rule** (`library/TrafficSpec/Rules/NRS_484B/NRS_484B_413_2.lean`) — binder class `ru_aggregate v "DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"`; applicability `.rises (drv_motion_turning v [p.turn_recognition_window, p.heading_change_noise_floor])`; obligation `asm → (100 ft duty)` ∧ `¬asm → (300 ft duty)`, each duty being `yaw_rate > 0 → holdsFor .path d "v" (indicator left ∨ arm left)` conjoined with the mirror for a negative rate. The hand is read at the judged observation, outside the window; the two feet figures are the text's own through `Units.feet`.

Two things worth flagging:

1. The gate enforces adapter-producibility that the Core files don't state: a scene's heading must equal the previous heading rotated by its yaw rate over the interval *before* it, and `kin.path_length` must grow by at least the chord between consecutive positions. That drove both failed runs; the final traces turn through the exactly representable unit heading (24/25, 7/25) with the yaw rate as `Units.millidegrees 32520`, so position, velocity, heading and path increment are exact and only the yaw rate carries a 0.0002° rounding.
2. I declared one narrowing of my own on s1: the hand comes from the *sign* of `kin.yaw_rate`, so an observation whose rate of change of heading is exactly zero has no hand and the duty is not stated there. Everything else I wrote is the record's reading, and the node needed no repair.
